detected_by: Operator question: whether finishing SD-31 could strand the 100% mandate on something not done in SD-30/SD-31. Confirmed by importing the dashboard producer's own doneness_verdict() and testing reachability per (wiring_class,status): ambiguous reaches done from NO status (2,109 units).
impact: A package split (SD-30 decisions.md §51) scheduled the engine-capability builds (SD-32) AFTER the grind lanes (SD-31) that cannot reach 'done' without them: 8,524 distinct units, 22.1% of the board, ceiling 77.9% without them. SD-31's completion gate additionally carried a per-cycle deferral hatch ('or named a successor for the remainder', twice) pointed at exactly those lanes — so SD-31 could have closed legitimately with the capability-blocked work deferred, SD-32 could then have built the capability, and the deferred work would have had to be reopened. Both packages stated the inverted dependency in their own text (SD-32 README: 'Unblocks SD-31 Epic 4-F3/F4... its contribution is unlocking SD-31's ceiling') without either drawing the conclusion. Caught before any SD-31 cycle fired; no work lost.
resolution: Operator ruling 2026-08-15: SD-32 absorbed into SD-31 and deleted; epics re-sequenced so capability (Epics 1-2) precedes the lanes consuming it; the two cross-package handoffs became internal per-batch hard gates; deferral hatch replaced by an operator-signed Structural Exclusion Register; standing reachability audit added as Epic 0.
summary: package split inverted a capability dependency and paired it with a deferral hatch
